The way I have done this in the past would be to take the hard drive out or boot from a live cd/usb stick. Attach an external drive and dd the entire drive to the external as an image. Then, install what you want, create the virtual disk, attach the external to the VM and dd that to the virtual hard disk.

Some caveats, though. You will need to shrink the C drive first because the size of the virtual disk you create should be the same as the old one. This may not work if there are UEFI options enabled.

Preperation

Items needed:

  • A linux live CD
  • A storage medium that is larger then the windows partition.

Steps Overview:

  • Connect storage medium, and boot live CD
  • mount storage medium
  • Use dd to copy windows partition Into a raw file on the storage medium
  • (Optional) Convert the raw file into another format, such as qcow2)

Operation

Connect storage medium, and boot a live Linux distribution.

In linux, mount the storage medium (DO NOT mount the windows partition)

Warning: dd is destructive and merciless, an entry error can be disastrous. Use this command to create a raw image of the windows drive

# dd if=/dev/sdX of=/mountedpath/on/storage/medium/file.raw conv=sync,noerror bs=64K

Where "/dev/sdX" is the windows drive, and "/mountedpath/on/storage/medium/file.raw" is the file on the storage medium. At this point, you have a raw binary representation of your windows file system.

Next, use fdisk to save partitioning information, most importantly, the cylinder size information. This is useful if you ever want to mount the filesystem from the raw file in linux.

# fdisk -l /dev/sdX > /mountedpath/on/storage/medium/filepartition.info

The raw file format can be used by qemu, but the disadvantage is that it will stay its current size (unless you want to edit its partition size, which is possibly dangerous). You can convert the raw file into the smaller and compressed qcow2 format by using: 

$ qemu-img convert -O qcow2 original-image.raw image-converted.qcow

I know that qemu supports both the reading of raw and qcow2, I am not familiar with other virtualization suits.
